articleBody:
Before your carpentry crew begins cutting baseboards, hanging closet doors, or building basement shelving, run through this practical checklist to avoid common moisture and fit issues.

- [ ] Slab moisture check — Confirm concrete floors and foundation walls are completely dry before delivering trim materials so wood does not cup or swell.
- [ ] Finished flooring thickness sample — Provide your carpenter with the exact flooring underlayment and plank thickness to ensure proper door clearances.
- [ ] Pressure-treated sill plate check — Verify all bottom plates contacting concrete use treated lumber or include a capillary barrier.
- [ ] Drywall floor clearance — Ensure drywall panels stop roughly half an inch above the slab to prevent moisture wicking behind baseboards.
- [ ] Utility access panel layout — Identify shutoff valves, cleanouts, and electrical panels so custom built-ins do not block code-required access.
- [ ] Rough opening squareness check — Measure door rough openings diagonally to confirm jambs will sit square without excessive shimming.
- [ ] Stair tread and railing measurements — Verify basement stairs meet local rise and run guidelines before ordering skirt boards or handrails.
- [ ] HVAC vent clearances — Check that planned baseboards and crown molding do not overlap return air grilles or supply registers.

How to use this checklist:
Walk your lower level with your tape measure and project plans before ordering interior finish lumber. Catching clearance gaps or dampness early prevents delays.
